text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Motorists will pay less vehicle taxes and receive rebates to offset charges they have to pay under electronic road pricing from early next year.
- Motorists will have to pay to use new second link and old Causeway between Singapore and Malaysia.
- National Trade Union Congress will approach employers to see if they are ready to raise retirement age before 1999, says union chief Lim Boon Heng.
- U.S Secretary of State Madeleine Albright says she shares ASEAN goal of integrating all 10 Southeast Asian countries as ASEAN an important player in maintaining region's peace and prosperity.
- Philippine government decides to postpone air talks with Singapore indefinitely following request from country's flag carrier Philippine Airlines.
- Singapore Airlines (SIA) exploring alternative arrangements with Tatas after Indian government kills plans for joint venture airline, says SIA Chairman S. Dhanabalan.
- Jurong Town Corp, through wholly-owned subsidiary JTC International, makes first direct investment in Philippines, US$150 million industrial park it will develop jointly with Filipino partners.

- German silicon wafer maker Wacker Siltronic AG is spending Singapore $478.5 million to build Singapore's first silicon wafer manufacturing plant, complementing nine fabrication plants in operation or being built.

- Electronics stocks continue to hog limelight, with hot favourite Venture Manufacturing rising S$1.15 to record intra-day high of S$8 before easing to S$6.90 for net gain of five cents due to weak general market sentiment.
- Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond submits resignation, Independent Television reports.
- IT researcher 25-year-old Chiang Kuo Chiang discovers flaw in latest version of most popular program used for accessing Internet, Netscape's Communicator web-browser.

- The Paragon on Orchard Road will soon get S$40 million facelift that will add nearly 10 percent more retail space, as well as S$85 million 14-storey tower extension housing medical suites and offices.
- Goldtron Ltd subsidiary Goldtron Holdings finds buyer for preference shares it will issue to finance purchase of China battery-making joint venture.
- Spire Technologies -- subsidiary of Sesdaq-listed Flextech Holdings -- is going into research and design of wafer probe cards with help from National Science and Technology Board.
- Mould-base maker Lung Kee Metals says it expects to boost revenues 10 percent within two years of operation after new Guangzhou plant starts up early next year.
